incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING @ana on-call for high latency: multiple alerts for p95/p99 on /v1/chat/stream. Alert group: canary-rollout-latency.
joel: seeing this too — started ~09:02 UTC after the canary roll (model v2.3-canary). p95 jumped to ~380ms -> 1.4s, p99 to ~2.9s. Streaming stalls reported.
nana (typo in name intentionally avoided)

nana: ignore (typo)
nana: sorry, false insert

joel: starting over: @ana — logs attached below.
ana: hey team, on it. grabbing dashboards.
ana: timeline: 09:00 UTC — canary rollout v2.3 started at 10% traffic; 09:01 UTC — canary percent bumped to 15% by autoscaler; 09:02 — first latency alerts.
marta: confirmed p95/p99 spike on console. p95 for streaming endpoint moved from 420ms to 1.2s, p99 from 980ms to 3.1s. Non-streaming /v1/chat/generate looks okay. Embeddings unaffected.
emily: customers are reporting UI stalls for chat, some sessions show infinite spinner, we have 5 support tickets so far. severity: moderate.
luis: grabbing canary pods logs. seeing repeated "KV cache miss + sync stall" on v2.3 containers with many small requests. suspect KV cache thrash under new attention caching pattern.
ops-bot: Deploy event: user-triggered rollout model-v2.3-canary by @ai-release at 08:59:47 UTC. Canary percent changed: 0% -> 10% -> 15% (09:01:05 UTC).
nana: quick check — is the canary using the new compilation kernel that touches batched KV state?
luis: yes, v2.3 has kernel-opt-3 enabled that changes KV layout. On some sequences KV cache management triggers syncs that block streaming worker thread for ~200-800ms periodically.
joel: what mitigations can we take immediately? options: reduce canary percent, route streaming off to stable model, rollback canary, or flip kernel flag remotely if supported.
nana: we can flip a runtime flag to disable kernel-opt-3 for canary via config service: PATCH /configs/model-v2.3?disable_kernel_opt=1 — will require rolling config and restart of canary pods (fast).
luis: downside: restart will drop KV warm cache -> temporary higher latency for a few minutes but should remove stalls.
emily: customer comms — propose we post an incident banner: "We’re investigating increased chat latency for a subset of customers. Mitigation in progress."
marta: agree. I'll open status page entry and notify support.
ops-bot: runbook suggestion: Step 1: reduce canary percent to 0% immediately to stop new traffic. Command: `redwoodctl rollout set-percent --deployment model-v2.3-canary --percent 0`
joel: executing reduce canary now. `redwoodctl rollout set-percent --deployment model-v2.3-canary --percent 0`
ops-bot: acknowledged. Canary percent set to 0% at 09:12:08 UTC. Traffic should begin draining.
luis: verifying pod metrics — requests to v2.3 dropped to near zero, but existing canary pods still finishing inflight requests and some residual stalls observed.
ana: while traffic drains let's also set a temporary routing rule to pin streaming requests to model-v2.2-stable explicitly: `POST /routing/override { "route": "/v1/chat/stream", "model": "model-v2.2-stable" }`
joel: applied routing override at 09:14:03 UTC.
emily: support notified, status page updated: "Mitigation: rolling back canary and routing streaming to stable. Latency improvements expected within minutes." :white_check_mark:
luis: after rollback/override p95 dropped back to ~450ms within 6 minutes. p99 trending down to ~1.1s. No new customer reports after 09:22 UTC.
marta: good. We should keep monitoring for 30m to ensure no regression and start postmortem.
nana: assigning postmortem owner: @luis. Please capture root cause, timeline, what allowed kernel-opt-3 to be enabled for canary without KV load test, and action items (increased canary ramp checks, KV stress, feature gate for kernel toggles, healthcheck for streaming tail latency).
luis: will own. Preliminary root cause: kernel-opt-3 changed KV cache locking semantics; under small-request high-concurrency streaming pattern this induced blocking syncs on the worker thread causing tail stalls.
joel: note for SLOs: impact window 09:02–09:20 UTC. Estimated affected requests ~0.8% of overall traffic (because canary percent peaked at 15% and streaming subset ~5% of overall). Suggest customer impact severity: low-medium, but UI-visible for some sessions.
emily: we'll offer affected customers a post-incident email and optional session replay logs on request. Support will prepare templates.
marta: handing off to next on-call @marta -> @joel at 10:00 UTC for watch. Oncall handoff: keep watches on p95/p99 for /v1/chat/stream for next 2 hours.
nana: also add a regression alert: if p99 > 1.5s for 5m on streaming after 09:30, auto-trigger rollback-fallback.
luis: added alert rule at 09:28:50 UTC.
joel: closing channel action items summary: rollback completed, routing override to stable applied, status page updated, postmortem owner assigned, follow-up action items: add KV stress to canary tests, add runtime feature gate, refine canary ramp automation.
emily: thanks team. I'll coordinate customer comms and postmortem distribution.
incident-bot: Incident resolved: canary-induced latency spike (model-v2.3-canary). Severity: P2. Opened postmortem: PM-5401 assigned to luis.
marta: marking this thread resolved. If anything flares up ping #eng-oncall. :thumbsup:
joel: leaving notes for retrospective: make canary build pipeline include a simulated streaming workload.
luis: will draft timeline and root cause writeup in postmortem doc.
emily: upload support ticket list to postmortem.
ops-bot: closing incident channel thread at 10:00:30 UTC per oncall confirmation.
(End of thread)
